extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, examiners and IP practitioners interacting with the Indian Patent Office
extracted.subtask_description: Practical manual of Office practice and procedure for filing, prosecuting, examining and post-grant management of patent applications under the Indian Patents Act and Rules. Covers filing formalities, patentability standards, examination, oppositions, post-grant procedures and related administrative requirements in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'invention'
rubrics_metrics.description: "invention" means a new product or process involving an inventive step and capable of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2(1)(j). This is the statutory threshold for subject-matter that can be claimed as a patentable invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (statutory definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "inventive step" means a feature of an invention that involves technical advance as compared to the existing knowledge or having economic significance or both and that makes the invention not obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2(1)(ja). Used in examination to determine non‑obviousness; see Chapter 8 (08.03.04) for principles and determination of inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capable of industrial application
rubrics_metrics.description: "capable of industrial application', in relation to an invention, means that the invention is capable of being made or used in an industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 2(1)(ac). Required along with novelty and inventive step for patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable mere discoveries/new properties/new use
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or of the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless such known process results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on borderline cases where mere discovery or mere use/property does not establish patentability (see also Section 3(d) discussion). Examiner should look for enhancement of efficacy, new product or a new reactant/step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant entitlement / who may apply
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made by the true and first inventor, the true and first inventor’s assignee, or the legal representative of a deceased true and first inventor or his/her assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6, 134, 135. Applicant must disclose name, address and nationality of true and first inventor. If inventor is not the applicant, proof of right (endorsement on Form 1 or assignment deed) must be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution on death or cessation of legal entity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant dies or a legal entity ceases to exist before grant, a person entitled by assignment/agreement or operation of law may request substitution by filing Form-6; Controller may allow substitution subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03.01.01. Controller will not issue substitution directions unless (i) invention identified in agreement by reference to application number, or (ii) acknowledgement that assignment relates to invention is produced, or (iii) rights finally established by court decision. For joint applicants, substitution requires consent of all joint applicants unless Controller directs otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial jurisdiction / appropriate office
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be filed at the Patent Office having appropriate territorial jurisdiction determined by (i) place of residence/domicile/business of applicant (first-mentioned), (ii) place where invention originated, or (iii) address for service in India if applicant has no place of business/domicile in India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 74, Rule 4. Indian Patent Office functions from Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai with specified territorial allocations. Appropriate office for divisional is office of main application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognised types: Ordinary Application (filed directly in India), Convention Application (directly or via PCT), Divisional Application, Patent of Addition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S. 7, 54, 135. Each type has specific filing requirements, priority considerations and processing paths (see Chapters 6 & 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory contents of a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application should contain: Form-1 (application), proof of right (endorsement or assignment), provisional/complete specification (Form-2), Form-3 (Section 8) if applicable, Form-5 (declaration as to inventorship) where required, power of authority if filed through agent, priority documents if applicable, signatures and dates, drawings signed, and where biological material from India is used — permission from National Biodiversity Authority and source of geographical origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 7, Rule 8 and related provisions. Provisional specification cannot be filed for Convention applications. Fees vary based on pages/claims (First Schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: E‑filing requirements and process
rubrics_metrics.description: E‑filing permitted; applicant/agent must register, have a digital signature, download client software to generate XML, upload signed XML (max 15 MB), complete EFT and print acknowledgement/CBR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 6 and 03.04.02. Objectives: save time and protect priority dates. Office upgrading e‑filing to accept subsequent papers electronically; procedures and user manual available on IPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes and deemed dates for leaving/serving documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents may be tendered by hand, post, registered post, speed post, courier or electronic transmission duly authenticated; if sent by post/courier/electronic transmission they are deemed filed at the time the mail would have been delivered in ordinary course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 6. In postal/courier delay, deemed date rules apply. Controller may condone delays on petition immediately after receipt with evidence, up to the period between intended and actual receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving documents in Office (fee/non-fee counters and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and documents are received at separate counters: Fee Counter (FC) and Non-Fee Counter (NFC). Counters close at 5 pm; fee documents produce Cash Book Receipts (CBRs), non-fee documents are entered in document receipt module; hourly transfer to EDP for digitization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03.04.04. Ensure correct counter and timing to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, paper size and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be written or typewritten or printed in Hindi or English, legible, on one side of A4 paper, with margins at least 4 cm top/left and 3 cm bottom/right; desirable line spacing 1.5 or double, non-script fonts like Arial/Times/Courier, font size 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 9. Signatures not legible or in other script must be accompanied by transcription in Hindi or English in block letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If application discloses nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings, they shall be filed in electronic form; fee payable with respect to equivalent number of pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 9. Use electronic format and pay fees per First Schedule equivalent pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees may be paid in cash, electronic means, bank draft or cheque; fee payable must accompany the document; fee deemed paid on date draft/cheque would reach Controller; fee once paid is not refundable; different fee scales for natural persons vs others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 142, Rule 7, First Schedule. Where application processed by a natural person is transferred to non-natural person, differential fee must be paid with transfer request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing of applications (digitization and numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt, Office accords date and serial number; PCT national phase and non‑PCT applications have separate serial numbers; documents are digitized and forwarded to relevant sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03.05.01. Proper initial processing is prerequisite to subsequent examination/search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are ordinarily published within eighteen months from date of filing or priority or within one month from request for early publication; particulars of publication and effects are prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 4 (04.01-04.04). Applicant may request early publication; withdrawal before publication possible within 15 months under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination — timing and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for examination must be filed ordinarily within forty-eight months from date of filing or priority, whichever is earlier; exceptions where secrecy directions or other provisions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11B, Rule 24B and 21.02. Controller ordinarily refers application to examiner within one month of publication or request for examination. Certain time limits are non-extendable and some special cases allow different timings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination standards: novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination includes search and assessment of novelty, inventive step (general principle and determination) and industrial applicability; also considers whether invention falls into statutory non‑patentable categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 08.03.01–08.03.06. Examiner issues report; Controller considers examiner's report and issues FER. See specific chapters for guidance on determination of inventive step and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Examination Report (FER) timing and compliance period
rubrics_metrics.description: FER is ordinarily sent within six months from request for examination or publication; applicant has twelve months from FER date to comply with requirements imposed by the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 24B(3) and 24B(4). The examiner's report will identify objections and requirements — timely responses required to continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and extension of time (petition for extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits for various acts are prescribed in Act/Rules; Controller may extend a time limit by one month on petition under Rule 138, except for some non-extendable provisions (e.g., Rules 24B, 55(4), 80(1A) etc.). Requests for extension must be made before expiry of prescribed period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 21.01–21.02. Rule 138 generally allows only one month extension; other specific rules may allow different extensions where expressly provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of a claim / priority documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority claims must comply with Paris Convention/WTO and PCT provisions; priority documents (if required) must be submitted within prescribed time (often three months from Controller's communication unless otherwise provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 05.04 and 07.01. Priority may involve multiple priorities and special rules for multiple/ cognate priorities (see Chapter 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional and complete specification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete specification must include title, field of invention, prior art and problem to be solved, objects, summary, detailed description, drawings, abstract, best method, and claims; provisional specification and content rules apply where provisional is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5 (05.01–05.03). Filing complete specification within twelve months from provisional filing is mandatory; claims must be clear and unity respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best method and sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete specification must disclose the invention sufficiently and include the best method known to the applicant for performing the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 05.03.11 and 08.03.07. Sufficiency of disclosure is grounds for objection/revocation if the specification does not enable a person skilled in the art to perform the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: structure, clarity, unity, scope and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be clear in structure and scope, show unity of invention and their significance and scope must be indicated in the specification; clarity and unity are examined and may be objected to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 05.03.12–05.03.16. Examiner will raise objections on lack of clarity, lack of unity, or improper scope; applicants should draft claims to meet statutory/office expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications and patent of addition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional applications arise from division of a parent application and must be filed/processed in conjunction with main application; patent of addition may be filed for an improvement or modification and has specific novelty/inventive step considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 6 (06.01–06.02). Appropriate office for filing divisional is office where main application filed; divisional priority and fees rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convention applications, PCT international and national phase requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Convention applications, PCT international applications and PCT national phase entries have specific documents, time limits and requirements; Indian Patent Office acts as receiving office under PCT in prescribed circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 7 (07.01–07.03). Includes requirements for international search, preliminary examination, fees, withdrawals and national phase entry (31-month standard) and other formalities (Rule 20 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-grant opposition procedure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-grant opposition may be filed any time before grant of patent; patentee/applicant receives notice and has specified time to respond (reply statement and evidence within three months from Controller's notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 08.06 and Rule 55. Pre-grant opposition considered before grant; Controller decides after proceedings and may issue report/decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant opposition procedure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant opposition must be filed within one year from date of publication of grant; patentee has two months from receipt of opponent's statement to file reply; subsequent evidence timelines are prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9 (09.01–09.03), Rules 58–59. Opposition Board submits report ordinarily within three months from forwarding documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of patent: compliance, consequences and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant is subject to compliance with conditions under the Act; grant brings into effect patentee rights, co-owner rights, certain exceptions where patent rights are not infringed, and defines term of patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 08.07.01–08.07.08. Controller records grant, patent date, and conditions; rights and limitations spelled out in the Act and manual comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance, renewal fees and restoration of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal (maintenance) fees must be paid within prescribed years; first renewal is before expiry of second year for third year; restoration of lapsed patents has procedure and time limits (application within eighteen months from date patent ceased to have effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 10 (10.01–10.03) and 21.03 table (items 35–41). Extensions for payment have maximums (e.g., six months under certain rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Working of patents — statements and furnishing information
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee must furnish information relating to working of patent for each calendar year within three months from year end and furnish particulars upon notice of Controller within two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 146(2), Rule 131(2) and 21.03 entries 46–47. Information relates to exploitation and is relevant for compulsory licensing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licensing grounds and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licence provisions (Section 84 et seq.) include grounds such as reasonable requirements of the public not being met; applications must contain prescribed contents and follow specified procedure and terms; related patents and export licences have particular provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 13 (13.01–13.02). Includes special provisions for pharmaceutical exports in certain circumstances and termination rules for compulsory licences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent for purposes of Government and acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Central Government may exercise powers to use inventions for government purposes, acquire inventions, and determine rights of third parties; procedures and consequences are prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 14 (14.01–14.05). Includes rights of third parties and reference of disputes to High Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and conduct of patent agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent agents' registration, disqualifications, rights, restrictions on practice, duties (subscription/verification) and grounds for refusal or removal of name from register are set out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 15. Rules specify Form requirements, examinations, restoration of names and Controller's powers to deal with agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offences and penalties under the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Various offences (contravening secrecy directions, falsification of register entries, unauthorized claim of patent rights, misuse of 'Patent Office' words, refusal/failure to supply information, practice by non-registered persons, offences by companies) attract penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 16 lists specific contraventions and related consequences; enforcement provisions must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: General powers and discretionary powers of the Controller
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller has powers analogous to civil courts, to award costs, review, correct clerical errors, exercise discretion in directions, refuse to deal with certain agents, remove names of agents, and make ex‑parte decisions where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 17 (17.01–17.09). Controller must record reasons where powers are exercised; procedural safeguards apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and supply of copies of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication (and after grant) the application, complete specification, provisional specification, drawings and abstract may be inspected at the appropriate office; copies/certified copies are available on payment of prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 18.04 (Rule 27, Section 72, 147). Register of Patents may be inspected during working hours on written application with fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific advisers: roll, qualifications and removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller maintains a roll of scientific advisers (names, qualifications, signatures, photographs, disciplines, experience) for the purpose of Section 115; qualifications generally include degree and at least 15 years' practical or research experience; Controller may relax qualifications; removal possible for misconduct or conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 19 (19.01–19.04), Rule 103–104. Roll updated annually and available on Office website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits and exhibits — evidentiary practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence in proceedings before Controller is ordinarily by affidavit unless Controller directs otherwise; affidavits should be confined to facts within deponent's knowledge (except interlocutory matters) and sworn in prescribed manner; exhibits copies must be supplied to other parties or originals left with Controller for inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 20.01 (Affidavits) and Rule 127 (Exhibits). Affidavit formalities differ for evidence taken outside India (diplomatic/consular officers, notary, judge or magistrate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing to be in public
rubrics_metrics.description: Where hearing before Controller of any dispute relating to an application or patent takes place after publication of complete specification, hearing shall be in public unless Controller directs otherwise after consultation with parties present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 139. Parties may request otherwise but Controller has discretion to direct private hearing on reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency / Power of Attorney practice (Form-26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorisation of an agent shall be in Form-26 or power of attorney; service upon agent is deemed service upon principal; as practice, an application may be accepted initially without POA to save priority, but subsequent papers require Form-26 or authorised power of attorney on record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 20.05. No office action is undertaken without Form-26/authorisation on record. Where a general POA is on file, an attested copy may be filed for subsequent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements and transcription
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatures must be legible; if signature is not legible or written in a script other than Hindi or English, it must be accompanied by a transcription of the name in Hindi or English in block letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 8 (Signature). Specifications and drawing sheets must bear signature/date as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy directions and inventions relating to atomic energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain applications may be subject to secrecy directions (e.g., national security/atomic energy) and have consequences for processing, filing abroad and request for examination timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03.05.03–03.05.04 and 21.03 table (item 16). Secrecy directions may pause certain time limits and alter procedures; periodical review every six months where secrecy direction is in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of biological material and biodiversity permission
rubrics_metrics.description: If application pertains to biological material obtained from India, applicant must submit permission from the National Biodiversity Authority before grant; application shall indicate source of geographical origin of biological material where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 03.04.01 (item 8–9) and Section 6 of the National Biodiversity Act, 2002. Permission must be submitted any time before grant, but it is sufficient if submitted before grant.
